parts.contentJson: {"text":"# PROJECT: PETROLEUM DEPOT MANAGEMENT — WEB ADMIN DASHBOARD  ## 1. Role and objective  Act as a senior SaaS product designer, enterprise dashboard UX specialist and accounting software interface designer.  Design a complete, high-fidelity, clickable web administration panel for a Petroleum Depot Management System.  The depot purchases petrol and diesel through tanker vehicles, stores fuel in multiple tanks, loads fuel into outgoing vehicles, sells fuel for cash and credit, collects payments, pays suppliers and monitors profit/loss.  The Android application is used by depot workers for daily transactions. This web dashboard is used mainly by the owner, manager and authorized accountant.  The dashboard must provide complete business visibility without requiring advanced computer skills.  Do not create a generic admin template or a collection of disconnected screenshots. Create a coherent application with a consistent design system, realistic sample data, reusable components and connected workflows.  Build a Figma Make prototype with functional navigation and interactive elements wherever supported.  ## 2. Design philosophy  The interface must be: - Professional and trustworthy. - Easy for nontechnical business owners. - Clean, modern and highly readable. - Focused on actual business operations. - Consistent across all modules. - Suitable for daily use on a Windows desktop or laptop. - Responsive on tablets and smaller browser windows.  Avoid excessive charts, unnecessary animations, tiny text, overcrowded tables, decorative gradients and complicated navigation.  Every screen must make its main purpose obvious.  Use clear written labels rather than relying only on icons.  ## 3. Frame and layout specifications  Primary design viewport: 1440 × 900 px.  Also test responsive layouts at 1280 × 800 px and 1024 px wide.  Create: - Fixed or collapsible left navigation sidebar. - Top header with page title, global search, notifications, connection status and user profile. - Main content area with consistent spacing. - Breadcrumbs on nested screens. - Responsive tables and cards. - Readable empty, loading, error and offline states.  Use Auto Layout and reusable components throughout the design.  Recommended spacing system: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24 and 32 px.  Use a 12-column grid where useful.  ## 4. Visual design system  Brand: Petroleum Depot Management.  Style: modern industrial business SaaS.  Colors: - Deep navy: primary navigation and important headings. - White: main surfaces. - Light slate gray: background and dividers. - Petroleum green: successful operations and healthy stock. - Blue: informational status and secondary actions. - Amber: warnings and pending operations. - Red: errors, overdue balances and stock shortages.  Use restrained color and strong contrast.  Typography: - Inter or a similar highly readable sans-serif. - Main page headings: 26–30 px. - Card headings: 16–20 px. - Key metrics: 28–36 px. - Table text: 14–16 px. - Form labels: 14–16 px. - Secondary descriptions: 13–14 px.  Use consistent currency formatting in PKR and explicit litre units.  All status badges must include text. Never use color alone to indicate a problem or successful operation.  ## 5. Application navigation  Create the following left sidebar navigation:  1. Dashboard 2. Tanks & Stock 3. Purchases 4. Loading & Sales 5. Customers & Udhar 6. Suppliers & Payments 7. Cashbook & Expenses 8. Profit & Loss 9. Reports 10. Daily Closing 11. Users & Devices 12. Sync Center 13. Backups & Recovery 14. Depot Settings  Use recognizable icons and short labels.  Highlight the current section clearly.  Provide a collapsible sidebar without hiding essential information.  At the bottom of the sidebar, show: - Depot name. - Local server connection indicator. - Current user role.  ## 6. Admin dashboard home  Create an executive dashboard for the current day with a date filter and clear reporting period.  Top header: - Page title: Depot Dashboard. - Depot name. - Reporting date. - Global search. - Notification bell. - Local server status. - Cloud sync status. - User profile and role.  First row: six summary cards.  1. Petrol Stock — total litres. 2. Diesel Stock — total litres. 3. Today's Sales — net sales revenue. 4. Today's Collections — payments actually received. 5. Customer Udhar — total outstanding receivables. 6. Supplier Payables — total outstanding liabilities.  Use realistic sample values, clearly marked as demonstration data.  Each card should have a small descriptive label and an optional link to the relevant detailed page.  Second row: - Fuel stock by tank. - Today's purchase and loading activity. - Sales and collections comparison.  Third row: - Gross profit. - Net profit. - Operating expenses. - Cash balance. - Pending approvals.  Do not confuse sales revenue with cash collected.  Do not calculate profit by subtracting today's cash receipts from today's purchases.  Show a clear note indicating when reports contain provisional transactions or stale data.  Quick action buttons: - Record Purchase. - Record Loading. - Receive Payment. - Pay Supplier. - Record Expense. - View Daily Closing.  Recent activity table: - Date and time. - Transaction number. - Transaction type. - Customer or supplier. - Fuel type and litres when applicable. - Amount. - Payment status. - User. - Posting status.  ## 7. Tanks and stock management  Create a tank overview page with tank cards and an optional table view.  Each tank card must display: - Tank name and ID. - Fuel type. - Capacity in litres. - Current book stock. - Percentage of capacity. - Minimum stock level. - Last physical reading. - Stock discrepancy. - Status: Normal, Low Stock, Reconciliation Required or Attention Needed.  Use horizontal fill-level indicators with accessible labels.  Tank details page: - Current calculated stock. - Physical measured stock. - Difference between measured and book stock. - Estimated inventory value. - Receipts and loading history. - Transfers. - Approved adjustments. - Stock movement chart. - Physical reading history.  Actions: - Record Dip Reading. - Transfer Fuel. - View Movements. - Request Stock Adjustment.  Stock adjustments must require permission and a reason.  A physical reading must not silently change the inventory ledger.  Create a stock reconciliation screen showing the recorded balance, measured balance, difference and required approval.  ## 8. Purchase management  Create a purchase register with: - Purchase voucher. - Supplier. - Invoice number. - Incoming tanker registration. - Fuel type. - Destination tank. - Invoice litres. - Actual received litres. - Purchase rate per litre. - Additional charges. - Total landed cost. - Amount paid. - Outstanding amount. - Date. - Status.  Filters: - Date range. - Supplier. - Fuel type. - Payment status. - Receipt status.  Actions: - New Purchase. - View. - Print. - Export. - Record Payment. - Request Correction.  Purchase creation form should use clear sections:  Supplier and invoice details.  Incoming vehicle and delivery information.  Fuel type, destination tank and quantity.  Purchase rate, freight, taxes and other applicable costs.  Payment terms and amount paid.  Final review and confirmation.  Clearly flag differences between invoiced and physically received litres.  Prevent duplicate posting and show whether the transaction is locally pending, accepted by the local server or synchronized with the cloud.  ## 9. Loading and sales management  Create a loading register showing: - Loading ticket. - Sales invoice. - Date and time. - Customer. - Destination vehicle. - Driver. - Source tank. - Fuel type. - Litres loaded. - Selling rate. - Invoice total. - Amount received. - Outstanding amount. - Operator. - Posting status.  Provide filters for date, customer, vehicle, fuel type and payment status.  Actions: - New Loading. - View Invoice. - Print Loading Ticket. - Receive Payment. - Export Report.  New loading workflow: 1. Select fuel type. 2. Select source tank and show available stock. 3. Select customer or cash customer. 4. Select destination vehicle. 5. Enter verified loaded litres. 6. Enter selling rate. 7. Review invoice amount and estimated cost where authorized. 8. Select payment terms. 9. Review all details. 10. Confirm posting.  Show a warning if the proposed loading exceeds available stock or requires additional approval.  Do not permit a posted transaction to be silently edited or deleted.  ## 10. Customers and udhar  Create a customer directory with: - Customer code. - Name. - Phone number. - Credit limit. - Total invoiced. - Total paid. - Outstanding balance. - Overdue balance. - Last transaction.  Customer detail page: - Account summary. - Invoice history. - Payment history. - Outstanding invoice list. - Credit notes. - Unallocated advances. - Statement and ageing report.  Payment allocation workflow: - Select customer. - Enter payment amount. - Select payment method. - Allocate to one or more invoices. - Show allocated and unallocated amounts. - Review. - Confirm. - Generate receipt.  Support partial payments.  Show overdue balances using clearly labeled badges.  Provide: - Add Customer. - View Account. - Receive Payment. - Print Statement. - Export.  Never mark an invoice fully paid unless the accounting allocations support that status.  ## 11. Suppliers and payables  Create a supplier register with: - Supplier name and code. - Contact details. - Purchases. - Total paid. - Outstanding payable. - Overdue amount. - Last purchase.  Supplier detail: - Purchase invoices. - Payment history. - Advances. - Returns and credits. - Outstanding invoice ageing. - Account statement.  Supplier payment workflow: - Select supplier. - Enter amount. - Select cash or bank account. - Allocate payment to invoices. - Review. - Confirm. - Print payment voucher.  Distinguish the purchase expense or inventory value from the later payment settlement.  ## 12. Cashbook and expenses  Create a cash and bank management module.  Display: - Opening cash. - Cash receipts. - Cash payments. - Bank receipts. - Bank payments. - Expenses. - Expected closing balance. - Actual counted cash. - Discrepancy.  Support: - Expense categories. - Expense date and reference. - Payment method. - Description and notes. - Attachment placeholder. - Entered-by user. - Approval status.  Expense form: - Category. - Amount. - Payment account. - Date. - Description. - Reference number. - Review and save.  Do not count a payment twice if it has already been recorded against a customer invoice, supplier invoice or expense.  ## 13. Profit and loss  Create a dedicated Profit & Loss page with: - Reporting period. - Comparison with previous period. - Net sales. - Cost of goods sold. - Gross profit. - Operating expenses. - Other applicable costs and income. - Net profit or loss.  Provide: - Petrol profitability. - Diesel profitability. - Fuel-wise margins. - Customer-wise profitability. - Sales-wise profitability. - Expense breakdown. - Trend chart.  Show the calculation definitions and reporting period.  Use inventory cost allocation rather than assuming that all litres purchased during the period were sold.  Distinguish accrual-based profit from cash flow.  When data is incomplete or transactions are still provisional, show an explicit warning.  Provide Print PDF and Export Spreadsheet actions.  ## 14. Reports  Create a reports center with clear report cards:  - Daily Depot Summary. - Purchases Report. - Sales Report. - Fuel Movement Report. - Tank Stock Report. - Stock Reconciliation Report. - Customer Outstanding Report. - Supplier Payables Report. - Cashbook Report. - Expense Report. - Profit & Loss Report. - Vehicle Loading Report. - User Activity Report. - Daily Closing Report.  Each report should support: - Date range. - Relevant filters. - Preview. - Print. - PDF export. - Spreadsheet export.  Show a clear empty state if no records match the filters.  Report totals must be derived from the same transaction ledger used by the application.  ## 15. Daily closing  Create a guided daily closing workflow.  Display: - Opening cash. - Cash sales. - Customer collections. - Supplier payments. - Expenses. - Other cash movements. - Expected closing cash. - Actual cash counted. - Difference.  Also show: - Opening stock. - Receipts. - Loading. - Adjustments. - Calculated closing stock. - Latest physical measurements.  Require the authorized user to review discrepancies before finalizing closing.  Allow the owner to configure closing rules.  A closing record must not prevent late-arriving offline transactions from being silently ignored. If a transaction arrives after closing, flag it and support an auditable reopening or adjustment workflow.  ## 16. Users and devices  Users page: - Name. - Login identifier. - Role. - Status. - Last activity. - Assigned depot. - Device association.  Roles: - Owner. - Manager. - Operator. - Accountant.  Allow authorized administrators to invite or create users, assign permissions, disable access and revoke sessions.  Device page: - Device name. - Device identifier. - Assigned user. - Authorization status. - Last local server connection. - Last cloud sync. - Pending transactions. - App version.  Do not display sensitive credentials.  A revoked device must be blocked from server operations once it reconnects.  ## 17. Synchronization center  Create a dedicated Sync Center.  Show three separate statuses: - Local database and local server. - Internet and cloud connection. - Cloud backup freshness.  Display: - Last successful sync. - Pending transactions. - Accepted transactions. - Rejected transactions. - Conflicts requiring review. - Failed sync attempts. - Last successful backup.  Use plain-language messages.  Example states: - Connected to Depot. - Internet Unavailable — Local Operations Continue. - 12 Transactions Awaiting Cloud Sync. - 1 Transaction Needs Review. - Cloud Backup Overdue.  Provide: - View Pending Items. - Review Conflict. - Retry Synchronization. - View Sync History.  Do not use a generic green Online indicator when the cloud is disconnected.  Do not let users resolve conflicting financial or stock transactions by blindly overwriting the latest record.  ## 18. Backup and recovery  Create a backup administration page.  Show: - Last successful local backup. - Last successful cloud backup. - Backup file size. - Integrity verification status. - Retention policy. - Next scheduled backup. - Last restore test.  Actions: - Create Backup. - View Backup History. - Verify Backup. - Restore Backup. - Export Encrypted Backup.  Restoration must require elevated permissions and a clear confirmation process.  Show the backup timestamp and recovery point before restoring.  Never report success before the operation has completed and been verified.  Include a warning when no recent off-site backup exists.  ## 19. Depot settings  Create settings sections: - Business Profile. - Fuel Types. - Tanks. - Invoice Numbering. - Currency and Rounding. - Time Zone. - Users and Permissions. - Devices. - Local Server. - Cloud Connection. - Printing. - Reports. - Backup Retention.  Use simple forms with clear save and cancel actions.  Separate ordinary configuration from sensitive security settings.  ## 20. Search, filters and tables  Implement reusable data tables with: - Readable column headings. - Sorting. - Pagination. - Search. - Date filters. - Status filters. - Clear empty states. - Row-level actions. - Export.  Keep important financial columns visible at normal desktop widths.  Use responsive alternative layouts when tables become too wide.  Provide a global search for customers, suppliers, invoices, loading tickets and vehicles, subject to the current user's permissions.  ## 21. Notifications and alerts  Create a notification center for: - Low stock. - Tank capacity warnings. - Stock discrepancies. - Overdue customer payments. - Overdue supplier payables. - Credit-limit breaches. - Failed synchronization. - Conflicts requiring review. - Cloud backup overdue. - Failed backup verification.  Each notification should have a clear description, severity and action link.  Avoid unnecessary notifications for normal daily activity.  ## 22. Prototype interactions  Connect all major screens and workflows.  Required prototype paths:  Dashboard → New Purchase → Review → Saved Purchase.  Dashboard → New Loading → Review → Saved Loading.  Customers → Customer Details → Receive Payment → Receipt.  Suppliers → Supplier Details → Pay Supplier → Payment Voucher.  Tanks & Stock → Tank Details → Record Dip Reading → Reconciliation.  Cashbook → Record Expense → Confirmation.  Profit & Loss → Date Filter → Report Preview.  Daily Closing → Cash Reconciliation → Review Discrepancies → Confirmation.  Users & Devices → Revoke Device → Confirmation.  Sync Center → View Conflict → Review and Resolve.  Backups → Create Backup → Verify Status.  Use interactive filters, tabs, dropdowns, modals, confirmation dialogs and date-range selectors wherever supported.  Do not create buttons that look functional but have no meaningful prototype action.  ## 23. Design system and components  Create reusable components for: - Sidebar navigation. - Header. - KPI cards. - Stock indicators. - Status badges. - Data tables. - Filters. - Search bars. - Date pickers. - Form fields. - Dropdowns. - Primary and secondary buttons. - Confirmation dialogs. - Toast notifications. - Empty states. - Loading states. - Error messages. - Offline banners. - Sync indicators. - Charts. - Report cards. - User and device rows.  Use consistent component naming and Auto Layout.  Use accessible contrast and clear focus states.  ## 24. Required Figma pages  Organize the design file into:  01 — Cover and Product Overview.  02 — Design Tokens and Typography.  03 — Reusable Components.  04 — Dashboard.  05 — Tanks and Stock.  06 — Purchases.  07 — Loading and Sales.  08 — Customers and Udhar.  09 — Suppliers and Payments.  10 — Cashbook and Expenses.  11 — Profit and Loss.  12 — Reports.  13 — Daily Closing.  14 — Users and Devices.  15 — Sync Center.  16 — Backups and Recovery.  17 — Depot Settings.  18 — Prototype Flows.  19 — Empty, Error, Offline and Conflict States.  ## 25. Realistic demonstration data  Use clearly labeled fictional data for prototype examples.  Example: - Depot: Main Petroleum Depot. - Fuel types: Petrol and Diesel. - Tank A: Diesel, 12,000 L capacity. - Tank B: Petrol, 10,000 L capacity. - Currency: PKR. - Customer accounts: Cash Customer, Transport Company A and Transport Company B. - Supplier accounts: Supplier A and Supplier B.  Do not connect the prototype to actual customer data or live financial services.  Ensure that sample calculations are internally consistent.  ## 26. Final quality requirements  The final output must be a polished, coherent, clickable web admin design.  Prioritize: 1. Clear navigation. 2. Readable stock and financial balances. 3. Correct separation of sales, cash collection, receivables and payables. 4. Easy transaction review. 5. Reliable offline and synchronization status visibility. 6. Safe financial corrections. 7. Consistent reusable components. 8. Desktop usability with responsive behavior.  Do not stop at the dashboard. Complete all major screens, workflows, error states and prototype connections.  Deliver a Figma Make project that a developer can use as the visual specification for the actual React/TypeScript web admin application.","providerOptions":{}}
